newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin sacks sauna-scandal justice minister.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin sacks sauna-scandal justice minister.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin on Wednesday sacked his justice minister, who had been allegedly filmed cavorting in a sauna with three naked women.
Valentin Kovalyov was replaced by a former national security chief, Sergei Stepashin, a Kremlin spokesman said.
Yeltsin suspended the minister a week ago pending a probe into a newspaper report that said he had been filmed in a gangland sauna with naked women in 1995.

Interior Ministry officials have said the grainy video film, sections of which have been broadcast on Russian television, was genuine. It was not clear whether the sacking meant the investigation was formally over.
Kovalyov, 53, has implied the film is fake. He had asked Yeltsin to suspend him to give him time to clear his name.
The Kremlin spokesman said Yeltsin had signed two decrees on the matter. That on Kovalyov simply said he had been "relieved of his duties".
Itar-Tass news agency said Yeltsin took the decision -- the first time a minister has been sacked in such circumstances -- during a meeting with Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin on Wednesday.

Sackings prompted by allegations about the private lives of ministers are all but unknown in Russia and -- typically -- this case has prompted more discussion and intrigue about the source of the video tape than the alleged transgressions.
For Stepashin, a former head of of the FSB federal security service, it was a return to prominence after a spell behind the scenes.

Yeltsin sacked Stepashin, 45, in June 1995 for mishandling a hostage-taking crisis in the southern Russian town of Budennovsk. At least 120 people were killed in the stand-off, and separatist Chechen fighters who took the hostages subsequently escaped.
Stepashin has headed the government's administrative department since November 1995. He is married and has one son.
